title: ReSyn: Autonomously Scaling Synthetic Environments for Reasoning Models
data_curation: ReSyn replaces (Q,A) pairs with (Q,V) question-verifier pairs produced by a five-stage pipeline run entirely with Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 (max_tokens=8192, temp=0.7). (1) Keyword extraction yields ~100 seed keywords drawn from BBH and KOR-Bench subtasks plus manually added algorithm/data-structure terms. (2) Task synthesis prompts the LLM 8x per keyword to write Python environments implementing instance generator rho_0, observation O, and reward R. (3) A two-stage LLM-as-judge enforces reference-free verification and computational advantage, plus well-specified questions; failures are revised and re-evaluated. (4) Instance generation samples n instances per difficulty level d in {1..5}. (5) Difficulty calibration solves each Q and keeps only environments with significant negative solve-rate/difficulty correlation (one-sided Wald test, alpha=0.05). From ~100 keywords, 418 environments survive, yielding 16K training and 500 validation (Q,V) pairs, matching SynLogic's scale. Semantic-entropy analysis shows ReSyn is 8-15 points more diverse than SynLogic.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. The only curriculum-like element is the per-environment difficulty parameter d in {1..5} used during instance generation and calibration, with instances split uniformly across levels; training itself is a single RLVR stage with no warmup/anneal schedule, no SFT or preference stage, and no cross-stage data mixing.
method: ReSyn's core contribution is autonomously synthesizing diverse reasoning environments for RLVR by exploiting the generator-verifier gap: the LLM specifies how to check a solution (a code verifier R:SxA->{0,1}) rather than solve it, enabling tasks beyond the teacher's solving ability. Each environment is a tuple (S,A,R,O,rho_0) where rho_0(d,n) generates instances at difficulty d, O renders natural-language questions, and R programmatically verifies answers. Training uses the open-source DAPO recipe on verl with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as policy (chosen over base to retain instruction following). RLVR samples G candidates a_i~pi(.|Q), computes reward r_i=V(a_i) times a format score, and updates via GRPO advantages with clip ratios 0.2/0.28, no KL penalty (kl_coef=0), dynamic sampling that filters all-correct/all-wrong groups, an overlong-buffer penalty, lr=1e-6, 16 responses/prompt, and 400 steps. Prompts force  tags and <answer> formatting.
eval_metrics: Benchmarks: Big-Bench Hard (BBH), Big-Bench Extra Hard (BBEH), GSM8K-test, and AIME 2024, all zero-shot at temperature 0.8, top-p 0.95. Primary metric is mean@4 (mean@128 for AIME); BBH also reported at 0/1/3-shot. BBEH subtask gains use paired bootstrap tests (alpha=0.01); dataset diversity uses LLM descriptors, sentence-transformer embeddings, hierarchical clustering, and Shannon semantic entropy. Headline: ReSyn-7B reaches BBH 75.2 (vs Instruct 65.9, SynLogic 66.5; +14% rel.), BBEH 14.3 (vs 11.2, +27% rel.; vs SynLogic 8.0), GSM8K 91.4 (vs 82.3), AIME 2024 14.0 (vs 9.8, +40% rel.). Ablations: Verifier-RL 75.24/14.61 vs Code-RL 74.94/14.24 vs Answer-RL 68.83/14.33 (BBH/BBEH); task-diversity scaling (N=400,M=40) gives 75.19 BBH vs 69.85 (N=100) and 71.20 (N=25).
key_results: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct + ReSyn (DAPO, 400 steps): BBH 75.2 (+14% rel. vs 65.9), BBEH 14.3 (+27% rel. vs 11.2), AIME 2024 14.0 (+40% rel. vs 9.8), GSM8K 91.4 (vs 82.3). It also beats SynLogic-7B on BBH (75.2 vs 66.5) and BBEH (14.3 vs 8.0), with verifier-based supervision and task diversity both shown as significant drivers via ablation.
evolution_note: ReSyn builds on the RLVR wave (DeepSeek-R1, OpenAI o1) and procedural reasoning environments (SynLogic, TinyZero, Reasoning Gym), but automates environment authoring via LLM-synthesized code verifiers, scaling task diversity >10x beyond SynLogic's 35 handcrafted tasks and exploiting the generator-verifier gap. In the 2026 landscape it points toward labor-free, self-scaling reasoning curricula for continued RL post-training without manual task engineering.
